page.layout: One printed page (left-hand page 594 of the scan). Running head at top: "LIBRI IV." centred and "Analysis" at right. One main text column, with marginal notes in the left margin ("Monachi mendicātes.", "Aleatores.") and two small margin marks (a circle and a caret) beside the text. The strip at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: ctant[?], & mille artes, mendacia, dolos atq; impo-sturas fingunt, ut aliis pecuniā emunctis,& veris pauperibus, qui ipsis debetur, bolo è faucib. ere-pto,non occulte tantum, sed publice quoq; fur-ta,imo sacrilegia committunt. Quos quidem divinæ & humanæ leges seuerissimè coerceri vo-lunt, quemadmodum in Politia nostrâ ecclesia-sticâ lib.2.c.19.ostendimus.

Monachi mendicātes.Talis est monachorum quoque mendican-tium ordo, qui verè, ut ille dixit,pauperes sunt sine defectu, quíque[?] religionem quæstui haben-tes, sub longarum orationum prætextu,domos viduarū penitus comedunt & devorant, quem-admodum Christus Matth.23.v.4. de hypocritis affirmat, cùm tamen ipsi quoque Canones mo-nachum absque opere & labore non esse velint,non tam propter victus necessaria, quàm propter animæ salute, ne vagentur perniciosis cogitationibus, & ad instar for-nicantis Ierusalem,omni transeunti divaricet pedes suos, quemadmodū dist.5.de consecrat.c. Nunquam, habetur. Et Socrates lib.4.hist.eccl.c.18.religio-si cujusdam dictum refert,qui dixerit,Monachum, si non laboret,pro fraudatore habendum esse,adeoq;pro fure.

Aleatores.Pertinent huc etiam aleatores, & qui talis at-que tesferis utuntur, & pecunias suas, quibus fa-miliam alere,& pauperibus consulere debebant, perfidè illis suffurantur, casui atque fortunæ lu-dibrio illas exponentes, & pecunias suas turpiter disipando , illarum non dominos,sed tyrannos, & profusores prodigos agunt. Ex hac aleâ qua-stum captatum,furti instar esse,usura victoriam,& fe-rarum

page.notes: Two marginal marks without text stand in the left margin: a small circle beside the line "viduarū" and a caret beside "affirmat"; they are reference marks, not transcribed as notes. The running head is printed as "LIBRI IV." (centre) and "Analysis" (right); both are given. Doubtful readings: "ctant" at the top (the first letter is an ornate ligature, possibly "stant"); "quíque" (accent unclear); the word "fure." may be roman rather than italic. Printed spacing such as "pto,non" and "dist.5" is copied as printed. The printed word "rarum" stands on its own line, right-aligned, and is the end of "fe-rarum".
